items.note: The page sets up S_Omega, the frames D_v, the edge changes D_vD_u^{-1} and D_in/D_out exactly as in the paper (lines 787-803), proves the invariant and reads off the implemented operator D_out S_Omega D_in^{-1}. It then explains why interior frames cancel ("edge changes telescope ... and gates let their frame through; they only set edge costs"), which matches the paper's conclusion at lines 823-825.

The page has every piece of the paper's induction: the logical input g=D_in^{-1}f with "no work is done"; the invariant holding at sources by definition; an edge turning "stored D_uφ into D_vφ"; and the gate step "∑_jc_jD_vφ_j=D_v∑_jc_jφ_j" with c_j∈R the same at every address. It concludes "By induction the invariant reaches the sinks, so the network implements D_out S_Omega D_in^{-1}", as in lines 804-817.

The page says S_Omega "moves the logical array g_w of w to role ρ(w) as ε_wg_w" and combines this with the identity to get ε_wD_sink(ρ(w))D_source(w)^{-1}, "scratch roles included". It names ρ correctly as swapping the banks and fixing the scratch roles (Lemma lem:scalar-motifs, line 1121), and it states that interior frames "only set edge costs", as in lines 818-825.
